citations.text: Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (2023). Behavioral science and education for sustainable development: Towards metacognitive competency. Sustainability, 15(9), 7413.

en.general: In the design concept, the practice of persisting with or changing one's behavior in line with chosen values, taken from the idea of psychological flexibility in contextual behavioral science. It is the second part of the metacognitive competency.

examples: Staying with a difficult conversation because it matters to you.
Dropping a habit that avoids discomfort but works against a value.
